office_does: The three Cowlitz County commissioners adopt the county budget, set county taxes and fees and pass county ordinances; the District 3 seat is nominated by district but elected by the whole county.
race_blurb: One-term Commissioner Rick Dahl, who cast the lone vote against the county's 2026 public safety sales tax, faces middle-school teacher Chelsea Chandler, a first-time candidate who wants the county to pursue grants and outside investment.

candidates.summary: District 3 commissioner since his 2022 election and a retired credit-union executive, running on opposition to tax increases and to new restrictions on property.
highlights: Cast the lone vote against the county's 2026 0.1% public safety sales tax, saying the county should cut spending instead [S4]
Says he has opposed every suggestion of a tax increase and any new restrictions on what owners can do with property [S2]
Called homelessness spending 'enabling' before voting with the board to accept an $11.7 million state homeless grant [S5]
Retired after 39 years at Fibre Federal Credit Union, latterly as senior vice president [S3]

taxes.basis: Repeated statements against any tax increase and a recorded no vote on the 2026 public safety sales tax.

spending.basis: Argues the county should reduce spending rather than raise revenue and calls homelessness spending 'enabling', though he voted to accept the state homeless grant.

experience.basis: Sitting commissioner seeking a second term after one term in office; long private-sector banking career.

candidates.summary: Monticello Middle School science teacher and former county health-program worker, a first-time candidate running on outside investment, housing affordability and family-wage jobs.
highlights: Says refusing outside funding leaves Cowlitz County behind and the county should compete for grants [S3]
Names affordable housing and family-wage jobs as the county's biggest challenges [S3]
Pledges decisions based on data and experts 'not on political ideology' [S3]
Former Peace Corps volunteer; managed Longview School District's Teen Parent Program [S2]
Endorsed by the Cowlitz County Democrats and the Cowlitz-Wahkiakum Central Labor Council [S4]

spending.basis: Wants the county to pursue grants and outside investment and 'invest wisely', paired with stewardship language and no specific new programs.

experience.basis: First-time candidate with no prior elected office, running as a working parent and teacher against the incumbent.
